statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 13 of 100 in the low band, twelve points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 83 and confidence high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ trades 29,239-29,244, up about 0.36%, and has pulled back roughly 30 points from a newly extended 29,272.00 session high, while Brent corrects 2.1% to $105.32 and the 10-year holds 4.942% below its 4.978% overnight peak, leaving tail at 13 and stress extreme at 83 into the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report.
body:
The new evidence this hour is that the pullback from the overnight top has widened. NQ trades 29,244.00 on one feed and 29,239.25 on a second, up about 0.36% against a 29,135.25 previous close, with the session high extended marginally to 29,272.00 and 29,270.75 respectively. That is only three or four points above the 29,268.75 high recorded an hour ago, while price now sits roughly thirty points beneath it against eleven to fourteen points at the last assessment. The 29,040.50 overnight low is unchanged, so the band stands at about 232 points with price near the upper third but no longer pinned to the extreme.

That distinction is the reason tail eases from 14 to 13. Holding near a session extreme is a genuine amplifier, but the extreme is being sold into rather than refused, which is the observable opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement structure that defines tail risk. One marginal new high followed by a widening retracement is ordinary two-way trade in an uptrending session, not a no-retracement path.

Cross-assets have continued to stabilise. The ten-year yield is 4.942%, essentially flat on the day and back below the 4.978% high printed in early Asian trading, after Reuters reported it reaching 4.97% and the two-year touching 4.596% overnight. The two-year is now 4.562%, up a little over a basis point but off its own 4.583% peak. Brent has corrected about 2.1% to $105.32 and WTI 2.0% to $100.45 after Brent reached roughly a four-month high near $110 with a weekly gain in the low teens. VIX is 17.68, down 0.90%, inside a narrow 17.50 to 17.71 overnight band. None of these is aligned with an equity melt-up, so the single amplifier remains isolated.

Stress stays extreme at 83, one point lower than the previous hour. The backdrop has not changed: a global bond selloff has carried the ten-year toward 5%, crude has traded above $100 for a third consecutive day on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz conflict, the European Central Bank raised rates on Thursday and warned on energy-driven inflation, and the STOXX 600 rose 0.3% to 637.60 while heading for its worst week since April. Markets price roughly a 70% probability that the Federal Reserve raises its benchmark to 3.75%-4% on 16 September, which would be the first increase since 2023. That combination is exactly the difficult, high-volatility environment stress is meant to capture, and under this framework it is scored separately from the price-path question.

The August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC is the last inflation input before that decision, with consensus near 3.3% to 3.4% headline year-on-year and 2.4% core. It is a checkpoint, not an automatic block: its importance and the dispersion around it are scored in stress and confidence, and tail will be revised on the observed post-release path rather than on the size of any surprise. The conditional forecast therefore peaks at 23 in the release slot and 22 across the cash open, both inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and decays through the afternoon on the assumption that retracements are granted.

Confidence holds at 89. Live NQ quotes are available from two independent feeds, real-time yields and VIX are current, oil is current, the calendar is verified against a primary calendar source, and the material overnight stories have been confirmed against reputable reporting. The shared cross-asset context file was outside its freshness window at this assessment time, so it was not used; the assessment rests on independently fetched live evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 08:00 UTC on 10 September to 07:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 9 and holds a 9 to 11 band through the European morning with the mode recorded as mixed. The single excursion sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to WATCH and neither reached the 25 block threshold. Tail then decayed as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close. From 22:00 UTC the overnight session normalised into a 11 to 15 band with mixed conditions, and the final two slots at 06:00 and 07:00 UTC record trend-up at tail 13 and 14 as the overnight advance extended. Stress never left the extreme band, running 81 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence held 84 to 89 throughout.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the rest of the 11 September session and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail starts at 13 on the observed widening pullback, holds 13 through the European morning and builds to 14 and 15 as the release approaches and quoted depth conditionally thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open where a post-event move is either confirmed or rejected. The 14:00 UTC slot carrying the preliminary Michigan release eases to 19 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly by then. The afternoon decays through 17, 15 and 14, lifts to 15 into the final pre-close hour and 18 across the 20:00 UTC weekly close where weekend positioning concentrates, then falls to a 5 to 7 floor for the closure hours that represents residual gap risk into the Sunday reopen rather than any intraday mechanism. Two slots are mapped to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold. Stress stays extreme through the U.S. session, peaking at 92 in the release slot, and decays into the elevated band across the weekend. Confidence eases from 89 to the low seventies as the horizon moves past the last observable quote.
